what_happened: The design job "Add design note: land jobs directly on host main via merge_tree" was rejected at the final verdict. One of six acceptance criteria was unmet: the note must list alternatives considered and rejected, conflict handling (merge_tree conflict, host main moving during landing), and rollback or migration from the local branch. The verifier raised one major finding and no blockers. In section 7 of docs/design/direct-main-merge-tree-landing.md, the handling for "Host main moves while landing" and "Two jobs land at once" depends on a push refusal that cannot happen. No failed checks are listed.
cause: Design jobs have no required step that checks a note's mechanism against the existing landing code before the note builds on it. The concurrency and race handling was written from an assumed push-refusal behavior, and nothing traced what the real push or ref update does when main moves or two landings overlap. Criteria check that sections such as conflict handling exist, not that the described failure path can occur. Only the verifier reads the code, at the end. This is the same weakness as the neighbouring landing-design jobs.
other_causes: The reading and plan likely did not require each failure-handling claim to cite the code or ref semantics that produces the refusal or conflict signal.
open_hypotheses: The fields do not show whether the host would refuse a non-fast-forward push in some configuration, or whether the note assumed the wrong ref-update mechanism. They also do not show how the unmet criterion relates to the major finding: whether the section is missing content or only wrong.
contradictions: Only one of six criteria was unmet, so the note does list alternatives and rollback; the gap is limited to the race handling, which the finding calls unsound rather than absent.
prevention: Add a required design-job step before the note is finished: every claim about what the code or host does (a refusal, a conflict, a race outcome) must name the code path or ref semantics that produces it, and a critic must check each such claim against the landing code. Each rule the note changes must be traced to the existing landing flow, with a stated concrete failure signal for every concurrency case. This would stop the whole class of design notes that rest on unchecked mechanisms or numbers.
proposed_request:
Revise docs/design/direct-main-merge-tree-landing.md section 7 so the handling of "Host main moves while landing" and "Two jobs land at once" rests on behavior the code and host really have. First read the current landing code and state exactly how a ref update or push behaves when main has moved, and whether it is refused. If no push refusal occurs, design the detection explicitly, for example a compare-and-swap ref update with the expected old value, or a re-check of main before the update, plus the retry path. For each case, name the code or host behavior that produces the signal. Keep the existing alternatives, merge_tree conflict handling and rollback or migration sections consistent with the change. Add a CHANGELOG.md entry. Acceptance:
- Section 7 names the real mechanism that detects main moving and two simultaneous landings.
- Each claim about a refusal or conflict cites the code path or ref semantics behind it.
- The note still lists alternatives rejected, merge_tree conflict handling, and rollback or migration from the local branch.
- CHANGELOG.md has an entry.
